 SAN ANTONIO - As evenings get darker after the end of daylight-saving time, the Texas Department of Transportation is urging drivers to be more alert for people walking, citing a spike in pedestrian crashes during the fall months.
 On Friday, TxDOT took to the streets with its 'walking billboards' campaign, aiming to encourage drivers and pedestrians to stay safe as they walked along Blanco Rd. from West Ave. to Vista Del Norte, near Churchill High School.
 TxDOT said the timing is especially important because daylight-saving time ended Nov. 1, creating less visibility during evening commutes. The agency noted October and November are the two months when pedestrian crashes are most likely to happen in Texas.
 Statewide in 2025, 694 pedestrians were killed and 1,387 pedestrians were seriously injured in traffic crashes in Texas, according to TxDOT. 
 In the San Antonio area this year, TxDOT reported 686 traffic crashes involving pedestrians, resulting in 78 pedestrian fatalities and 106 pedestrian serious injuries. Most of those crashes happened at night, the agency said.
 TxDOT also said 68% of pedestrian fatalities and serious injuries in Texas in 2025 occurred in the dark. The push is part of TxDOT’s “Be Safe. Drive Smart” campaign.
